title: Cooling System Component Map — 5.2L
introduction:
I use this drawing like a transit map for engine heat: identify a component in the table, find its callout, then follow the arrows through the connected circuit. The exploded layout separates parts for clarity; it is not an access or removal sequence.

Start with the radiator, lower radiator hose, thermostat housing and coolant pump. Then trace the engine passages, heater inlet and outlet branches, and the smaller connections to the degas bottle. The pump circulates coolant, the radiator releases heat to outside air, and the heater core uses coolant heat to warm the cabin. The degas bottle provides expansion space and helps separate air from coolant. The oil filter and its adapter are useful landmarks, but the filter’s job belongs to the lubrication system.

Arrow direction shows the illustrated coolant route; arrow color describes its temperature under the conditions in the note. These colors are a guide to understanding the circuit, not a temperature test or a verdict on a component. This map identifies the cooling arrangement for this engine; opening, draining, testing or repairing it requires the matching service procedure.

edits.text: NOTE: Coolant temperature changes with ambient temperature and engine load. This illustration represents an ambient temperature of 38° C (100° F). Red arrows show coolant over 82.2° C (180° F); Orange arrows show coolant at approximately 82.2° C (180° F); Blue arrows show coolant below 82.2° C (180° F).
edits.why: Read the colors as temperature bands for the illustrated operating conditions. A color on this map is not a measured temperature on your car, so it cannot by itself establish whether a hose, thermostat or pump is working correctly.
